overview: The two key variables in any controlled experiment — one is deliberately changed, the other is measured to see how it responds.
genZNote: Independent variable: what the scientist deliberately messes with. Dependent variable: what changes because of that meddling.

aspects.label: Role in Experiment
aspects.valueA: The variable that is deliberately changed or manipulated by the experimenter.
aspects.valueB: The variable that is measured/observed, expected to change in response to the independent variable.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Amount of fertiliser given to plants (set by the experimenter).
aspects.valueB: Plant height measured after a fixed time (the outcome being studied).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: In graphing convention, the independent variable always goes on the x-axis and the dependent variable on the y-axis — a very common practical-exam checkpoint.
overlay.memoryTrick: Independent = the cause you control. Dependent = the effect that 'depends' on it.
overlay.commonMisconception: Controlled variables (kept constant, like temperature) are a separate third category — they are not the same as either the independent or dependent variable.
